bug_semantics: ImportedClusterSecrets stores the complete imported Talos cluster secrets bundle, including CA private keys. The resource was placed in ResourceService's ordinary role-by-verb access branch, where Get/List/Watch require only Reader, so an authenticated Reader could retrieve those keys and use them outside Omni to obtain control of the imported Talos, Kubernetes, and etcd APIs.
flaw_origin: First-party authorization design error in the commit that introduced ImportedClusterSecrets: a highly sensitive secret-bearing resource was explicitly classified with ordinary Reader-readable resources instead of requiring Operator. The immediate parent contains neither the resource nor that access-list entry.
ai_marker: NONE: the BIC is authored and committed by Oguz Kilcan, has only his Signed-off-by trailer, and PR #1332 has one commit; no AI author, bot, Co-Authored-By, generated-by, or other AI marker is present on the BIC. The advisory's bugbunny.ai credit identifies the later discoverer, not the writer of the vulnerable lines.
evidence: Bundle SHA-256 is 25ec9d9616f720808b16b6077583cd5e5d914fa3cd6a2ba726ebab9d30c25a7a and its active GitHub advisory says Reader can retrieve ImportedClusterSecrets containing the full CA bundle; GitHub's advisory API reported withdrawn_at=null on 2026-08-30.

Commit f8de9a6d96453bf3e5b9f33668fa35169ada24c0 creates ImportedClusterSecretsSpec.data and client/pkg/omni/resources/omni/imported_secrets.go, and adds omni.ImportedClusterSecretsType to internal/backend/runtime/omni/state_access.go's ordinary resource case. That case calls auth.CheckGRPC(ctx, auth.WithRole(verbToRole(access.Verb))), while verbToRole maps Get/List/Watch to role.Reader. The same commit's auth test lists importedClusterSecret with all verbs and no admin/operator restriction.

Parent 753259c26edd3e1f61a98a69d334212fa7a9a03b has no ImportedClusterSecrets symbol in the targeted proto, resource, import, or state-access paths. Targeted all-ref -S history identifies f8de9a6d96453bf3e5b9f33668fa35169ada24c0 as the first addition of ImportedClusterSecretsType; the commit has exactly one parent.

GitHub commit-to-PR metadata maps the BIC to merged PR #1332. The PR reports commits=1 and merge_commit_sha=f8de9a6d96453bf3e5b9f33668fa35169ada24c0, so there is no smaller public PR member to decompose.

The BIC's full metadata names Oguz Kilcan as both author and committer and contains only Signed-off-by: Oguz Kilcan. Neither the BIC message nor PR #1332 metadata contains an AI marker. The advisory credits bugbunny.ai with discovery, which is remediation-era evidence and does not attribute the BIC.

Direct fix 25fa9e141ee00285e70210ed40d11e4e457c871d removes ImportedClusterSecretsType from the Reader-by-verb case and adds a dedicated auth.WithRole(role.Operator) case, with an operator-only authorization test. Its parent is 39ee2f01ea1debd1e0af7df96025c4f0da79bbf5.

The maintenance releases carry explicit cherry-picks of the direct fix: v1.6.6 contains b8ca100c4539ea83f0ac2e53dcd523e6e5b68111 while v1.6.5 does not, and v1.7.3 contains a224cb020f3aaca2bc21c3e32a38eb4a37e531e8 while v1.7.2 does not. Both cherry-pick messages name source commit 25fa9e141ee00285e70210ed40d11e4e457c871d and apply the same state_access.go authorization change. This matches the advisory ranges >=1.3.0,<1.6.6 and >=1.7.0,<1.7.3.
reasoning: The vulnerable capability and the insufficient Reader authorization are first written together in f8de9a6d96453bf3e5b9f33668fa35169ada24c0, and the immediate parent proves absence. A one-commit PR provides no hidden member history to substitute for that BIC. The direct fix changes exactly the decisive authorization rule from ordinary verb-based Reader access to Operator-only, and its two release-branch cherry-picks establish both patched tag boundaries. Because the BIC itself has only conventional human identity and sign-off metadata and no AI marker, the causal authorship verdict is NOT_AI; the advisory's AI-named finder is not evidence that AI wrote the vulnerable code.
remaining_gap: The CVE.org cveawg API endpoint for CVE-2026-45726 returned HTTP 404 on 2026-08-30, so no CVE.org record disposition was available. The repository/vendor GitHub advisory was nevertheless published, unwithdrawn, and corroborated by the direct fix and both patched release branches.
